trial_court: Court of Metropolitan Magistrate (NI Act) - 04, South District, Saket Courts, Delhi (Trial Court) in a complaint case titled as Kishan Veer Gupta v. Nemi Chand - CT. Case No. 9441/2017
case_name: Kishan Veer Gupta vs Nemi Chand on 7 February, 2026
facts_of_case: Kishan preferred a complaint case against Nemi under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 alleging that Nemi approached him for a friendly loan of ₹2,50,000. Nemi assured Kishan that he would return the same within a period of six months. Kishan arranged the sum from his relative and advanced it to Nemi as a friendly loan.

legal_principles.principle: A person who advances a loan to another, knowing that the borrower may not be able to repay it, cannot claim that the loan was for discharge of a legally enforceable debt.
legal_principles.held: The Trial Court failed to appreciate that no complaint was filed by Nemi about the cheques, particularly when Kishan refused to return the same to him on account of Kishan's failure to advance any loan to Nemi.
cited_cases: Kalamani Tex & Anr. Vs. P. Balasubramanian, (2021) INSC 679
Bir Singh vs. Mukesh Kumar, (2019) INSC 149

legal_principles.principle: A person who approaches another for a loan and is informed that some people can advance loans, but they will take security cheques as collateral, cannot claim that the loan was not for discharge of a legally enforceable debt.
legal_principles.held: Nemi handed over two blank signed cheques of (cid:130)2,50,000/- each as security cheques along with a copy of Aadhaar card to Kishan.

use_for_drafting: drafting an appeal against acquittal in a cheque bounce case
preparing a complaint case under the Negotiable Instruments Act
understanding the Code of Criminal Procedure and its application
